prompt: recommend me some laptops between $800 and $1500 for coding
text:
## Good laptop picks for coding in the **$800–$1500** range

Here are solid options depending on whether you want **Linux-friendly**, **best battery**, **best screen**, or **best value**.

### Top recommendations

| Laptop | Best for | Why it stands out | Typical price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MacBook Air M3 (13" or 15")** | Most developers | Excellent battery, silent, fast for coding, great trackpad/screen | ~$999–$1499 |
| **Lenovo ThinkPad T14 / T14s** | Linux + typing | Great keyboard, durable, business-class reliability | ~$900–$1500 |
| **Framework Laptop 13** | Upgradeability | Easy to repair/upgrade, very developer-friendly, good Linux support | ~$900–$1400 |
| **Dell XPS 13** | Premium Windows/Linux | Great build quality, compact, strong performance | ~$1000–$1500 |
| **ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED** | Best display value | Beautiful OLED screen, good performance, usually strong battery | ~$900–$1300 |
| **HP Spectre x360 14** | 2-in-1 flexibility | Nice screen, premium design, good for mixed use | ~$1100–$1500 |

---

## My short picks by use case

### 1) Best overall for coding: **MacBook Air M3**
Choose this if:
- you want **long battery life**
- you care about **quiet performance**
- you do web/dev, Python, Rust, JavaScript, mobile dev, etc.
- you don’t need GPU-heavy workloads

**Recommended config:**  
- **16 GB RAM**
- **512 GB SSD** if possible

> Avoid 8 GB if you multitask heavily or run Docker, IDEs, and lots of browser tabs.

---

### 2) Best Windows/Linux developer laptop: **ThinkPad T14s**
Choose this if:
- you want a **great keyboard**
- you use **Linux**
- you want a “workhorse” machine

**Look for:**
- AMD Ryzen versions if available
- **16 GB RAM minimum**
- 512 GB SSD

---

### 3) Best upgradeable laptop: **Framework Laptop 13**
Choose this if:
- you care about **repairability**
- you like to upgrade RAM/storage later
- you want strong Linux compatibility

This is one of the best “developer-first” laptops if you plan to keep it for years.

---

### 4) Best premium Windows ultrabook: **Dell XPS 13**
Choose this if:
- you want something sleek and portable
- you prefer Windows but may also run Linux
- you want a higher-end feel

**Note:** XPS machines are nice, but sometimes less comfortable for long typing sessions than ThinkPads.

---

### 5) Best screen for the money: **ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED**
Choose this if:
- you want a sharp, colorful display
- you do a lot of reading and UI work
- you want strong value

OLED looks fantastic, though you should consider possible burn-in risk if you leave static UI elements on screen all day.

---

## What specs matter most for coding

### Minimum I’d recommend
- **CPU:** modern Intel Core Ultra, AMD Ryzen 7000/8000 series, or Apple M-series
- **RAM:** **16 GB**
- **Storage:** **512 GB SSD**
- **Display:** 1080p or better; 14" is a sweet spot
- **Battery:** aim for 8+ real-world hours if you move around

### If you use Docker, VMs, or big IDEs
- **32 GB RAM** is worth it if you can get it under budget
- prioritize RAM over CPU upgrades

---

## Best choices by budget

### Around **$800–$1000**
- **ThinkPad E14 / T14 (sale prices)**
- **ASUS Zenbook 14**
- **M1/M2 MacBook Air** on sale
- **Framework 13 base config**

### Around **$1000–$1300**
- **MacBook Air M3**
- **ThinkPad T14s**
- **Dell XPS 13**
- **Zenbook 14 OLED higher configs**

### Around **$1300–$1500**
- **MacBook Air M3 with 16/512**
- **Higher-end ThinkPad T14s**
- **HP Spectre x360 14**
- **Framework 13 with better specs**

---

## My practical recommendation

If you want the safest picks:

- **Best overall:** **MacBook Air M3, 16 GB RAM**
- **Best Linux/Windows work laptop:** **ThinkPad T14s, 16 GB RAM**
- **Best long-term buy:** **Framework Laptop 13**
- **Best screen value:** **ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED**

If you want, I can narrow this down based on:
- **Mac vs Windows vs Linux**
- whether you use **Docker/VMs**
- your preferred screen size: **13", 14", or 15/16"**
- whether you want **lightweight**, **best battery**, or **best keyboard**
